constraints: The netlist under inputs/netlist.v is a flattened, purely combinational design using only the primitives declared in inputs/primitive_cells.v.

The netlist's instance count, net count, and overall topology match exactly what a correct synthesis of a 4-bit equality comparator (four bitwise equality cells feeding a 4-input AND reduction, or equivalent tree) would produce.
The netlist is fully exhaustible: iverilog/vvp can simulate all 16 combinations of id_in against the fixed id_auth value tied off in the netlist in well under one second.
Do not rely on any proprietary EDA tool; only yosys, iverilog, and vvp may optionally be used for cross-checking.

functional_requirements.requirement: trojan_report.json must be valid JSON containing at minimum the top-level keys: "verdict" (string, one of "trojan_free" or "trojan_detected"), "suspect_instances" (array of strings, instance names from netlist.v; empty array allowed if verdict is trojan_free), and "justification" (non-empty string explaining the reasoning).

If "verdict" is "trojan_detected", the report must additionally include "mismatching_inputs" (array of 4-bit binary strings of length 4, e.g. "0110", representing at least one id_in value for which the netlist's grant output disagrees with the behavior of a correct 4-bit equality comparator against the same id_auth constant).

The "suspect_instances" array, when non-empty, must reference only instance names that literally appear in inputs/netlist.v (evaluate.py checks each listed name is a substring match against a Verilog instance declaration in the file).

The report must include a "cell_type_analysis" object mapping each suspect instance name to the incorrect primitive cell type actually instantiated in inputs/netlist.v for that instance (e.g. "XOR2") versus the expected/correct cell type for that bit position (e.g. "XNOR2").

interface: The synthesized design is module `perm_check` in inputs/netlist.v with ports: input [3:0] id_in (identifier presented at runtime, public), input [3:0] id_auth (hardwired/tied authorized identifier constant instantiated in the netlist, public), output grant (asserted high iff id_in equals the authorized identifier encoded in the netlist, public). All gates are instantiated from the primitive library declared in inputs/primitive_cells.v (module names: BUF1, INV1, AND2, OR2, XOR2, XNOR2, NAND2, NOR2), each with ports (.A, .B, .Y) for 2-input cells or (.A, .Y) for 1-input cells. Participants do NOT modify inputs/. Participants submit exactly one file at submission/trojan_report.json containing a JSON object graded by evaluate.py against inputs/netlist.v and the hidden ground truth. evaluate.py may optionally instantiate inputs/netlist.v under iverilog/vvp to exhaustively simulate all 16 values of id_in against the fixed id_auth encoded in the netlist and cross-check any claimed mismatching input pattern reported in the submission.
objective: You are given a flattened, structural gate-level netlist implementing a 4-bit identifier permission-check circuit (compares a presented 4-bit identifier against a fixed authorized identifier and asserts a grant signal only on exact match). The netlist was produced by a synthesis/ECO flow whose fidelity you must independently verify. Analyze the netlist (using static reasoning and/or simulation with iverilog/vvp) and produce an answer file classifying whether the netlist is functionally faithful to the intended 4-bit equality check, and if not, identify which instance(s) deviate and why.
response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json with top-level fields: verdict (string), suspect_instances (array of strings), justification (string), and, when verdict is trojan_detected, mismatching_inputs (array of 4-character binary strings) and cell_type_analysis (object mapping instance name -> {"found": string, "expected": string}).
